---
title: "A history of Transformers"
subtitle: "From attention mechanisms to the Transformer architecture and modern LLMs"
lang: en
---

The Transformer did not emerge without predecessors. Its history combines attention mechanisms developed for neural machine translation, self-attention, large-scale training, and different objectives across model families. This selective timeline highlights milestones; it is neither exhaustive nor a claim of a single causal path.

## Timeline


1. **2014 — Attention for neural machine translation.** Bahdanau, Cho, and Bengio propose an attention mechanism that learns to align output elements with relevant parts of the input in a recurrent encoder-decoder model. This is not yet the Transformer, but an important precursor. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.0473).
2. **2015 — Attention variants for translation.** Luong, Pham, and Manning study several attention and scoring approaches between source and target states. [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.04025).
3. **2017 — The Transformer.** Vaswani and colleagues propose an attention-based architecture without recurrence or convolution in its central mechanism. The paper introduces scaled dot-product attention and multi-head attention. [Attention Is All You Need](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762).
4. **2018 — Two pretraining paths.** GPT popularizes generative pretraining with an autoregressive Transformer decoder; BERT uses a Transformer encoder and a masked-language objective. These approaches are not interchangeable: they structure accessible context and the learned objective differently. [BERT](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.04805) · [GPT technical report](https://openai.com/index/language-unsupervised/).
5. **2019 — Scaling and longer context.** GPT-2 studies text-conditioned generation and zero-shot transfer; Transformer-XL introduces mechanisms to handle dependencies beyond a fixed segment length. [GPT-2](https://openai.com/index/better-language-models/) · [Transformer-XL](https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.02860).
6. **2020 — Larger models and other modalities.** GPT-3 studies few-shot behavior at scale; Vision Transformer applies Transformer blocks to sequences of image patches. [GPT-3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.14165) · [ViT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.11929).
7. **2022 — Human-feedback alignment and conversational interfaces.** InstructGPT studies instruction tuning, including learning from human preference feedback. ChatGPT makes a conversational interface widely accessible; this is a diffusion milestone, not the invention of the Transformer architecture. [InstructGPT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02155) · [ChatGPT announcement](https://openai.com/index/chatgpt/).


## What the timeline should not imply

- **Transformer does not mean autoregressive LLM.** The 2017 paper presents an encoder-decoder architecture for translation; BERT uses an encoder and a masked prediction objective.
- **Attention predates the Transformer.** The 2017 paper assembles and reorganizes existing ideas into a coherent architecture; it did not invent the entire family of attention mechanisms.
- **Scale does not explain everything.** Data, objectives, tokenization, architecture, training procedure, and evaluation also shape observed capabilities.
- **A publication date is not proof of absolute priority.** This page selects a few pedagogical milestones and does not attempt to catalogue every parallel contribution.
